text:
incident-bot: P1 ALERT: gpu-pool prod-gpu (us-west-2) saturating after model rollout v28.4. queue_length=12400 -> peaked 24000, avg_token_latency=9.2s, errors(502/503)>3k. autoscaler status=FAILED (reason: pool_max_reached). Paging oncall. runbook: https://internal/runbooks/gpu-saturation

tereza: i'm oncall - joining bridge now. paging @sarah @reno @mike. severity P1. linking bridge: https://meet/bridge/4958000000 :phone:

sarah: looking at autoscaler and runtime. quick summary: v28.4 changed tokenizer+ctx-window packing which increased per-session kv entries ~3x. this pushed per-gpu memory usage over threshold -> prefill/backpressure and large queueing. autoscaler attempted scale but hit pool_max_nodes=48 and refused further grow. logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T03:12:45Z] autoscaler: request_scale(target=60) -> rejected (max_nodes=48)
[2026-03-15T03:13:02Z] runtime: kv_cache_entries/session=312 -> 948 (v28.3=310)
[2026-03-15T03:14:11Z] gpu0 OOM? reclaiming KV pages -> increased latency
```

mike: on the infra side, we can either bump max_nodes (fast) or rollback model rollout (safer). which do we want immediate? if we bump, we need capacity in region and to check cost/quotas.

reno: quota available in us-west-2 for +32 gpus, we can increase pool to 80 nodes but that will take ~6-9m to spin up. rollback can start instantly for traffic not fully rolled out. recommend: immediate partial rollback + short-term pool bump.

tereza: agree. start rollback for canary and divert traffic away from prod-gpu for heavy customers. callout: customers with high throughput are on prod-gpu routing. @lin please start customer comms.

sarah: executing rollback for v28.4 -> v28.3 (canary first). commands: 
```bash
rictl model rollback --model v28.4 --to v28.3 --percent 100 --priority immediate
rictl routing update --route default --fallback-model v28.3 --divert 30% --tag dedicated-pool
```
output: 
```
initiated rollback: job_id=rb-4958-01 status=started
routing: diverted 30% traffic to dedicated-gpu-pool
```

reno: simultaneously increasing pool max to 80: 
```bash
rictl pool update --pool prod-gpu --max-nodes 80
rictl pool scale --pool prod-gpu --target-nodes 64
```
output shows new provisioning started. ETA ~7m.

lin: CS update: we have 6 customers reporting latency/errors: AcmeCorp, BrightAI, EduNow, Shoply, OUSales, Maplytics. impact window: 03:10-03:32 UTC. reported symptoms: failed requests 502/503, long tail latency >10s. sent initial notify to AcmeCorp account team; they asked for ETA. I'll send an update now saying rollback in progress and mitigation steps. templates used: "incident-short-update".

sarah: metrics after initial rollback/diversion (03:21 UTC): queue_length dropped from 24k -> 7.6k, overall GPU util 99% -> 86%, throttles/sec dropped 3k -> 800. still high but trending. autoscaler now allowed to request scale (because we bumped max_nodes). new nodes provisioning.

mike: can we set temporary rate limits for anonymous / high-volume keys to reduce steady load while nodes come up? we have a quick config: 
```json
{"route":"/v1/generate","rate_limit_per_min":6000,"apply_to":"api_key_high_volume"}
```
apply and notify engineers.

tereza: applied rate-limit to top 10 high-volume keys. early effect: queue_length -> 5.2k at 03:27 UTC. thanks.

sarah: provisioning finished at 03:30 UTC, autoscaler added 18 nodes, pool at 66 nodes, per-gpu memory pressure gone. rollback completed to v28.3 03:33 UTC. full metrics: queue 24k -> 1.1k over 21 minutes, 95th latency back to baseline ~220ms, error rate <0.2%.

lin: customer comms update sent at 03:35 UTC to all 6 affected customers. message: we observed increased errors & latency due to model rollout; immediate rollback and capacity increases completed; monitoring for any regressions. support is following up individually.

reno: note - root cause appears to be an untested tokenizer packing change in v28.4 which increased kv cache growth for long-context sessions. rollout ramp was 30%/15m by default but telemetry didn't flag the extrapolated kv growth early enough. two immediate followups: (1) add a preflight check that measures kv entries per session vs baseline for a 1k sample, (2) set autoscaler soft-alert when pending queue >5k AND scale_request rejected for pool_max.

mike: taking on postmortem. action items I own: write rollback playbook for model rollouts, add canary telemetry for kv growth, implement autoscaler alerting, update rollout default ramp to 10%/30m for tokenizer/model changes. I'll create tasks in ENG-OPS and assign.

tereza: handing off oncall to mike for the remainder. i'm stepping off the bridge. @mike you're the incident lead for postmortem.

mike: ack handoff. will collate logs and create a timeline. please upload any user repro traces to the shared folder: /internal/incidents/4958000000/evidence

sarah: short root-cause note for postmortem: v28.4 tokenizer packing increased average kv entries/session by ~3x for long-context requests (>8k tokens). autoscaler hard cap + rollout ramp allowed regional saturation before we hit alerts. mitigation was rollback + pool max bump + targeted rate-limits. followups: preflight kv test, add synthetic long-context workload to CI, add rollout guardrails.

lin: CS closed loop: all affected customers acknowledged update; three requested credits for the downtime window, submitted to billing.

incident-bot: incident P1 resolved and bridge closed at 03:45 UTC. postmortem required. incident record: INC-4958. Please file postmortem within 72h. :white_check_mark:

mike: thanks all. I'll post the draft postmortem by EOD and schedule a follow-up blameless review.
